22.0.0.en: A pure river: not like the rivers of the world, which are clear at times and muddied at other times.

22.0.1.en: Clear as crystal: to stress its clarity and purity.

22.0.2.en: The meaning is of course spiritual, for there is no thirst and no drinking in the Kingdom of God. What is meant by the river and the water of life is the sweet divine consolations granted by God to His chosen ones, to those who love Him and to the heirs of eternity. For this reason he said that the source of the river is proceeding out of the throne. This description reminds us of the conversation of the Lord Christ with the Samaritan woman about the water of life, which whoever drinks of it shall never thirst (Jn 4:14).

22.1.0.en: In the midst of the street of it: an expression meaning the place that is open to all.

22.1.1.en: On either side: on both banks of the river.

22.1.2.en: St. John saw "the tree of life" on either side of the river. Some have held that this means a number of trees. But because the meaning is spiritual and symbolic in the first place, and because he used the expression "tree" and not "trees," we find that the meaning intended is that this tree is available and satisfying to all who dwell in the city, wherever their position on either side of the river.

22.1.3.en: The tree of life: most interpreters of the Holy Bible agree that the tree of life, available to all, is one of the expressions concerning the Lord Christ Himself, for He is the source of satisfaction for all who hunger and thirst after righteousness (Mt 5:6). Some have also held that the tree of life may be a type of the Cross.

22.1.4.en: And this "tree," that is, Christ, is abundant in gifts and graces to His children, and gives to them every month. He is not like the seasonal tree whose giving and fruit come once in the year, which is an indication of the continual satisfaction of the believers in their God. The expression "twelve manner of fruits" points to the richness, perfection and variety of these gifts. Since the year in our earthly understanding comprises twelve months, this means continuity throughout the year, that is, in the Kingdom forever.

22.1.5.en: And the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations: it is customary that the leaves of trees are gathered to be burned, but in the tree of life there is nothing unprofitable. Even its leaves are a source of consolation and rest, "healing," and the whole meaning is of course symbolic. By the nations are meant the believers from all the world, and not the Jews only.

22.1.6.en: The dear reader will not miss the contrast between this verse, in which the tree of life has become available to all, and what is said in the Book of Genesis (ch. 2:9), when it was hidden from men because of sin.

22.2.0.en: Since sin has completely passed away, and there is nothing unclean or defiled in heaven, where God is always present with His people, the first curse, which was because of sin, has also been lifted, and all its consequences, the toil of man and his suffering, have likewise been lifted, for eternal rest has begun. The source of this rest is the permanent presence of Christ "the Lamb." As for the heirs, "His servants," they spend eternity in the service of their God, with continual praise and glorification of His holy name, sharing with the angels in their heavenly work.

22.3.0.en: And they shall see his face: God said to Moses in ancient times, "there shall no man see me, and live" (Ex 33:20). Here the gift has become ours: after we are rid of the material body and rise with our bodies in a glorified form of light, we are able by it to see God face to face. This is the greatest gift that a spiritual man could desire. St. Paul also referred to this very scene when he said, "For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face" (1 Cor 13:12). His name shall be in their foreheads: an indication of belonging and attachment to God alone.

22.4.0.en: What is said in this verse agrees with what was explained in the previous chapter (v. 25): the absence of darkness and fear from the city of God, and no need for any created light such as the sun and the moon, because God will be everything to them and will make them need nothing else (see the commentary on ch. 21:25).

22.5.0.en: And he said unto me: the angel who was speaking to St. John.

22.5.1.en: These sayings are faithful: that is, everything you have seen and heard is true.

22.5.2.en: At the end of the scene of the vision of the city of God, the angel concludes his talk with St. John, assuring him that everything he saw and heard in this vision is true and genuine, and that the Lord God, in His good will, wished to reveal some of these scenes to His servants who are striving on earth, to encourage them to stand firm in the striving and resistance in which they are engaged, and so that their resolve may not fail before afflictions. He adds, reassuring them, that the appointed time for these things to happen is near and that its coming will be swift."

22.5.3.en: Yes, my God, we trust in Your promises, but at times we forget and our hearts become downcast, since we have set our ambition on the passing earth. But blessed is he whose eyes are fixed on heaven and on You, my Father, for he will have joy always here, and longing to meet You in Your heaven... O my God, how I long to see You!! Have mercy on me and make me one of those who have this portion.

22.6.s.en: (2) The conclusion of the book and the announcement of the coming of Christ

22.6.0.en: Behold, I come quickly: the words here are of the Lord Christ concerning His Second Coming.

22.6.1.en: As the book draws near its end, the Lord Christ reassures those who await Him, announcing His swift coming, and He also commends everyone who believed and whose heart clung to the words of the prophecies of the whole Book of Revelation.

22.7.0.en: I John: the saint pointed to his name to confirm the authority and truthfulness of the Book of Revelation.

22.7.1.en: Spiritual feelings reached their utmost and filled the being of St. John after all that he had seen and heard, and he found himself (especially after hearing the last voice of Christ) going down on his knees, "I fell down," to worship before the feet of the angel who had been his guide in this vision. But the angel prevented him from doing so, giving the reason: that he (the angel) is of God's creation, which worships Him and glorifies Him like the rest of the prophets and saints, but worship must be offered to God alone.

22.8.1.en: The Lord Christ wanted everything the saint saw in the Book of Revelation to reach us, so the command came to him to declare to us everything he saw. The Lord also urges him to do this quickly, since the time of His coming has become near (v. 7).

22.9.0.en: Christ declares that the time of repentance has ended with the end of earthly time and the beginning of eternity at His Second Coming. So everyone who is "unjust" will be repaid according to what he did, and everyone who defiled his body by sin will remain as he is. There is no longer any room to correct or change conditions... And just as the state of the wicked will remain as it is.. so also the state of the righteous.., for everyone who lived in righteousness, purity and holiness will remain as he was. That is, eternity is an extension of what a person sowed in his life on earth, and this makes clear to us the following truths:

22.9.1.en: (1) That God's wide mercies have as their sphere the life of man on earth, but what a person dies upon determines his final destiny.

22.9.2.en: (2) God is perfectly just, and so He repays the wicked and the righteous according to what they have done, without partiality.

22.9.3.en: (3) This verse carries a warning about the final destiny of man and urges him to repent before opportunities are lost.

22.10.0.en: Behold, I come quickly: what is meant is His Second Coming (v. 7). My reward is with me: this means that I alone am the giver of recompense and repayment, and the Judge (ch. 11:18). To give every man according as his work shall be: this expression is repeated in (Mt 16:27), (Rom 2:6), (ch. 2:22), and it is a proof of the divinity of the Lord Christ, that He is the just Judge.

22.10.1.en: Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last: these words also came in (ch. 1:8, ch. 21:6), and their meaning is the affirmation of the divine attributes of the Lord Christ, such as that He is the source and Creator of all things and that He is the eternal and everlasting God. He spoke of Himself with such attributes at the beginning of the book, and here He speaks with the very same attributes at its end, to declare to us that it is He who allowed John this vision and that He Himself is its subject and its essence.

22.11.0.en: That they may have right to the tree of life: that is, worthy to enjoy eternal life.

22.11.1.en: Here comes the promise of lasting happiness for the heirs of eternal life (the tree of life). This worthiness is made to rest on keeping God's commandments and doing them. For entering heaven is not by faith only, but also by striving to carry the commandment into practical life and to do it. This reminds us of what the Lord Christ Himself said: "If ye love me, keep my commandments" (Jn 14:15).

22.12.0.en: As for those driven out, who have no right to enter the city or to come near its gates, they are the dogs: everyone who persecuted the Church with his barking or tore at her flesh.

22.12.1.en: Sorcerers: everyone who had power through the dragon or the beast (Satan.) Likewise also those whose bodies the lusts have enslaved, such as the fornicators, and those who killed believers or unbelievers, and whoever worshiped anything other than God, whether money or position or self (idols), and whoever loved deceit or misleading or lying... For them there is no place in the city of God.

22.13.0.en: I Jesus: as the Lord said of Himself at the beginning of the book, "The Revelation of Jesus Christ"

22.13.1.en: (ch. 1:1), He comes here and affirms at the end of the book that the words are still His.

22.13.2.en: I have sent mine angel: what is meant here is the sending of St. John to us to inform us of what he witnessed and saw. To testify unto you: to inform you of the truth of these things.

22.13.3.en: I am the root and the offspring of David: that is, I am the Maker of David and his Creator, because I am God the Word, and by my Incarnation I became a man like you, of the offspring of David and his bodily descent.

22.13.4.en: This verse comes to ratify the whole Book of Revelation and to affirm its soundness. The Lord Christ Himself declares that it is He who allowed John to see all these heavenly visions so that the Church might know them in the various ages. It is He also who sent John to us and commanded him to write them (v. 10).

22.14.0.en: The Spirit: is the Holy Spirit.

22.14.2.en: Let him that heareth: every believer who hears what the Holy Spirit and the Church declare to him.

22.14.3.en: The Holy Spirit sets the hearts of the believers on fire, and likewise works powerfully in the Church, so that she bears the same call of the Holy Spirit to her children. All declare their longing for the moments of meeting with Christ and cry out from the depths of their being, "Come," and those who thirst after righteousness take and drink the fullness of the spiritual gifts freely, for the time of their striving and their labors has passed and the time of the divine reward has come.

22.15.0.en: These two verses carry a warning of the utmost severity from the Lord Christ Himself. He affirms, "I testify," that what is in this book, "the prophecy of this book," is His own word, and no human being is permitted to add to it a letter or to take anything from it. Whoever tries to do this, or comes near to attempting it, is subject to the following:

22.15.1.en: 1- The woes of God and His severe punishment, as came with the opening of some of the seals or the seven bowls in the book itself.

22.15.2.en: 2- His name is blotted out of eternity, so that he has no inheritance or portion, but is cast into the outer darkness, where is the lake of fire and brimstone, deprived of all the promises of the Book of Revelation promised to those who love the holy name of God.

22.16.0.en: He which testifieth: is the Lord Jesus Himself.

22.16.1.en: The Lord Christ, who is the faithful Witness, declares to us here that He responds to the call of the Church and the longing of all His believing children. When they cried out, "Come," His answer came reassuring and responsive, that His coming is certain and swift. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus: as soon as St. John heard these words from the mouth of the Lord of glory, his heart was set aflame and he answered the Lord, not for himself only but on behalf of all the believers, expressing our longings for eternity with his words, "Come, Lord Jesus."

22.17.0.en: St. John concludes his Revelation by invoking the grace of the Lord Jesus (the Giver of all grace) to be with the Church and all her believers in all the days of their earthly striving. After what we have witnessed in this whole book, how much we all need the work of God's grace in our lives, so that we may complete our striving and pass through the difficult times in the fear of God, also set aflame by His love, which always renews our longing to meet Him and to see His glory and the glory of His good Father and the Holy Spirit.

22.17.1.en: I wish that, amid the crowding of life and the dazzle of material lusts, you would not forget your goal, which is eternal life with Christ. So care for your relationship with God through prayers and spiritual readings, and the Holy Spirit will help you, giving you the Holy Mysteries and supporting you to complete your striving until you enjoy the Kingdom.

22.17.2.en: May the blessing of the prayers and intercessions of the beloved St. John be with us. Amen.
